claims.text: Complete Bloom-filter updates can be delayed or dropped when communication resources vary.
claims.poster_quote: Complete Bloom-filter updates can be delayed or dropped when communication resources vary, leaving stale state.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: When communication resources are constrained or time varying, complete-filter updates may be delayed or dropped, leaving stale receiver state.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that complete-filter updates may be delayed or dropped when communication resources are constrained or time-varying.

claims.text: Lossless compression offers one payload size.
claims.poster_quote: Lossless compression offers one payload size, while OR folding offers smaller queryable views with higher false-positive rates.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lossless compressed BFs reduce transmission size without changing membership behavior [6], but produce a single payload determined by the filter contents.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that lossless compression produces a single payload size.

claims.text: OR folding offers smaller queryable views with higher false-positive rates.
claims.poster_quote: Lossless compression offers one payload size, while OR folding offers smaller queryable views with higher false-positive rates.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: OR folding instead produces smaller, directly queryable views with increased FPR while preserving the no-false-negative property.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that OR folding produces smaller queryable views with higher false-positive rates.

claims.text: The largest qualified folded view is selected based on each communication opportunity.
claims.poster_quote: We select the largest qualified folded view supported by each communication opportunity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly describes the selection of the largest qualified folded view based on each communication opportunity.

claims.text: Paired traces compare adaptive folding with complete and compressed baselines.
claims.poster_quote: Paired traces compare adaptive folding with complete and compressed baselines.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Figures 4 and 5 report means and 95% confidence intervals over 20 paired traces of 500 opportunities, with all strategies using the same trace within each repetition.
claims.reason: Section IV.F, Evaluation Metrics: The paper explicitly mentions paired traces comparing adaptive folding with baselines.

claims.text: Adaptive folding does not universally beat lossless compression.
claims.poster_quote: Adaptive folding does not universally beat lossless compression; compression works when one representation is reliably deliverable.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: These results do not show that folding universally outperforms lossless compression.
claims.reason: Section VI, Discussion: The paper explicitly states that folding does not universally outperform lossless compression.

claims.text: Compression works when one representation is reliably deliverable.
claims.poster_quote: Adaptive folding does not universally beat lossless compression; compression works when one representation is reliably deliverable.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed lossless compression is effective when a single representation can be delivered reliably.
claims.reason: Section VI.B, Folding, Compression, and Deployment: The paper explicitly states that compression works when one representation is reliably deliverable.

claims.text: Folding helps when varying opportunities let a smaller qualified view prevent a missed update.
claims.poster_quote: Folding helps when varying opportunities let a smaller qualified view prevent a missed update.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Folding is useful when a fixed compressed payload cannot be supported but a smaller FPR-qualified view can.
claims.reason: Section VI.B, Folding, Compression, and Deployment: The paper explicitly states that folding helps when varying opportunities allow a smaller qualified view to prevent a missed update.

claims.text: Candidate ratios should match false-positive tolerance and channel conditions.
claims.poster_quote: Candidate ratios should match false-positive tolerance and channel conditions; folding and compression could be combined.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Candidate ratios should reflect the application’s FPR tolerance and anticipated communication conditions, and only qualified representations should be retained.
claims.reason: Section VI.B, Folding, Compression, and Deployment: The paper explicitly states that candidate ratios should match false-positive tolerance and channel conditions.

claims.text: Folding and compression could be combined.
claims.poster_quote: Candidate ratios should match false-positive tolerance and channel conditions; folding and compression could be combined.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The methods could be combined, although increased occupancy may reduce compressibility; this combination was not evaluated.
claims.reason: Section VI.B, Folding, Compression, and Deployment: The paper explicitly states that folding and compression could be combined.

claims.text: The example shows canonical query positions mapped into OR-folded views.
claims.poster_quote: The example shows canonical query positions mapped into OR-folded views.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Figure 2 illustrates the operation for two retained lengths. The example shows how the canonical query positions for one element are mapped into each folded representation.
claims.reason: Section III.B, OR-Based Bloom Filter Folding: The paper explicitly states that the example shows canonical query positions mapped into OR-folded views.

claims.text: The online policy selects using current communication conditions.
claims.poster_quote: The online policy selects using current communication conditions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that the online policy selects using current communication conditions.

claims.text: A fine-grained catalog comes from an unchanged canonical filter.
claims.poster_quote: A fine-grained catalog comes from an unchanged canonical filter.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity.
claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that a fine-grained catalog comes from an unchanged canonical filter.

claims.text: Retained lengths need not be integer divisors.
claims.poster_quote: Retained lengths need not be integer divisors.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: This work uses the same OR-folding principle but permits fine-grained retained lengths that need not be integer divisors of the canonical filter length.
claims.reason: Section III.B, OR-Based Bloom Filter Folding: The paper explicitly states that retained lengths need not be integer divisors.

claims.text: Evaluation covers two datasets and three channel models.
claims.poster_quote: Evaluation covers two datasets and three channel models.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Evaluation uses two phishing URL datasets and Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading models.
claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states that the evaluation covers two datasets and three channel models.

claims.text: PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish each use 5,000 malicious URLs inserted.
claims.poster_quote: PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish each use 5,000 malicious URLs inserted; 50,000 disjoint benign URLs provide absent queries.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion.
claims.reason: Section IV.A, Datasets: The paper explicitly states that PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish each use 5,000 malicious URLs inserted.

claims.text: 50,000 disjoint benign URLs provide absent queries.
claims.poster_quote: PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish each use 5,000 malicious URLs inserted; 50,000 disjoint benign URLs provide absent queries.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.
claims.reason: Section IV.A, Datasets: The paper explicitly states that 50,000 disjoint benign URLs provide absent queries.

claims.text: Classical targets 1% false positives.
claims.poster_quote: Classical targets 1% false positives; sparse targets 25% occupancy with three hashes.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For each dataset, the classical filter length m is selected for n = 5,000 elements and a target FPR of 1%.
claims.reason: Section IV.B, Bloom Filter Construction: The paper explicitly states that the classical filter targets 1% false positives.

claims.text: Sparse targets 25% occupancy with three hashes.
claims.poster_quote: Classical targets 1% false positives; sparse targets 25% occupancy with three hashes.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sparse canonical filter uses the same m, with its hash count selected for a target occupancy ρ = 0.25: ksparse = round(−ln(1 − ρ) * m/n). Equation (10) produces three hash functions.
claims.reason: Section IV.B, Bloom Filter Construction: The paper explicitly states that the sparse filter targets 25% occupancy with three hashes.

claims.text: Catalog views cap empirical false positives at 10% with zero observed false negatives.
claims.poster_quote: Catalog views cap empirical false positives at 10% with zero observed false negatives.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Only representations with no observed false negatives and an empirical FPR no greater than 10% enter the adaptive catalog.
claims.reason: Section IV.B, Bloom Filter Construction: The paper explicitly states that catalog views cap empirical false positives at 10% with zero observed false negatives.

claims.text: Baselines include uncompressed and losslessly compressed filters.
claims.poster_quote: Baselines include uncompressed and losslessly compressed filters; payloads use 480-byte packets with 32-byte headers.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sparse canonical bit array is compared with gzip [17], zlib [18], bzip2 [19], and LZMA [20]. Uncompressed classical and sparse filters are also included.
claims.reason: Section IV.C, Compression and Transmission Baselines: The paper explicitly states that baselines include uncompressed and losslessly compressed filters.

claims.text: Payloads use 480-byte packets with 32-byte headers.
claims.poster_quote: Baselines include uncompressed and losslessly compressed filters; payloads use 480-byte packets with 32-byte headers.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Payloads are segmented into 480-byte packets with 32-byte headers.
claims.reason: Section IV.C, Compression and Transmission Baselines: The paper explicitly states that payloads use 480-byte packets with 32-byte headers.

claims.text: Each trace has 500 opportunities of 10 ms.
claims.poster_quote: Each trace has 500 opportunities of 10 ms; results average 20 paired repetitions across Markov capacity, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh fading.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The experiments model complete-report delivery within individual reporting opportunities and do not separately model packet reordering. Each interval is a 10-ms transmission opportunity.
claims.reason: Section IV.E, Channel Models: The paper explicitly states that each trace has 500 opportunities of 10 ms.

claims.text: Results average 20 paired repetitions across Markov capacity, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh fading.
claims.poster_quote: Each trace has 500 opportunities of 10 ms; results average 20 paired repetitions across Markov capacity, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh fading.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Figures 4 and 5 report means and 95% confidence intervals over 20 paired traces of 500 opportunities, with all strategies using the same trace within each repetition.
claims.reason: Section IV.F, Evaluation Metrics: The paper explicitly states that results average 20 paired repetitions across the three channel models.

claims.text: Both URL datasets show nearly identical false-positive rates.
claims.poster_quote: Both URL datasets show nearly identical false-positive rates, indicating that occupancy and deterministic mapping primarily govern folding.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The two datasets produce nearly identical false positive rates across the evaluated ratios.
claims.reason: Section V.A, Bloom Filter Folding Tradeoff: The paper explicitly states that both URL datasets show nearly identical false-positive rates.

claims.text: Occupancy and deterministic mapping primarily govern folding.
claims.poster_quote: Both URL datasets show nearly identical false-positive rates, indicating that occupancy and deterministic mapping primarily govern folding.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Because both filters contain the same number of inserted elements and use the same construction parameters, this similarity indicates that folding behavior is governed primarily by filter occupancy and the deterministic position mapping rather than by one particular URL collection.
claims.reason: Section V.A, Bloom Filter Folding Tradeoff: The paper explicitly states that occupancy and deterministic mapping primarily govern folding.

claims.text: False-positive rates rise gradually under moderate folding, then accelerate near saturation.
claims.poster_quote: Rates rise gradually under moderate folding, then accelerate near saturation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The false positive rate increases gradually under moderate folding and then rises more rapidly as the reduced representation approaches saturation.
claims.reason: Section V.A, Bloom Filter Folding Tradeoff: The paper explicitly states that false-positive rates rise gradually under moderate folding, then accelerate near saturation.

claims.text: About 50% size reduction remains near the catalog limit, providing multiple accuracy-cost operating points.
claims.poster_quote: About 50% size reduction remains near the catalog limit, providing multiple accuracy-cost operating points.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Approximately 50% size reduction remains near the 10% maximum FPR used by the adaptive policy. The resulting valid representations provide multiple communication-cost and accuracy operating points.
claims.reason: Section V.A, Bloom Filter Folding Tradeoff: The paper explicitly states that about 50% size reduction remains near the catalog limit, providing multiple accuracy-cost operating points.

claims.text: Experiments isolate channel-driven selection but limit generality.
claims.poster_quote: Experiments isolate channel-driven selection but limit generality.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The controlled design uses two URL datasets at the same cardinality with fixed contents. This isolates channel-driven selection but does not establish generality across other workloads, cardinalities, occupancies, or changing contents.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that experiments isolate channel-driven selection but limit generality.

claims.text: Two fixed URL datasets share one cardinality, limiting workload generality.
claims.poster_quote: Two fixed URL datasets share one cardinality, limiting workload generality.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The controlled design uses two URL datasets at the same cardinality with fixed contents. This isolates channel-driven selection but does not establish generality across other workloads, cardinalities, occupancies, or changing contents.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that two fixed URL datasets share one cardinality, limiting workload generality.

claims.text: The controller assumes timely channel state.
claims.poster_quote: Controller assumes timely channel state; estimation error and metadata costs are unmodeled.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The controller also assumes timely communication-state information and does not model estimation error, delayed feedback, or metadata explicitly.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that the controller assumes timely channel state.

claims.text: Estimation error and metadata costs are unmodeled.
claims.poster_quote: Controller assumes timely channel state; estimation error and metadata costs are unmodeled.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The controller also assumes timely communication-state information and does not model estimation error, delayed feedback, or metadata explicitly.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that estimation error and metadata costs are unmodeled.

claims.poster_quote: No fixed-fold baseline is tested; one sender-receiver excludes contention, retransmission, and energy effects.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fixed folded representations are not included as baselines.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that no fixed-fold baseline is tested.

claims.text: One sender-receiver excludes contention, retransmission, and energy effects.
claims.poster_quote: No fixed-fold baseline is tested; one sender-receiver excludes contention, retransmission, and energy effects.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The single sender–receiver configuration also excludes contention, retransmission, congestion, and fairness effects.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that one sender-receiver excludes contention, retransmission, and energy effects.

claims.text: Future work should study changing contents, measured channels, multiple senders, and combined folding/compression.
claims.poster_quote: Future work should study changing contents, measured channels, multiple senders, and combined folding/compression.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Priorities for future work are direct comparison with fixed folded baselines; integration with cardinality/FPR-driven resizing [7]; and evaluation with changing contents, measured channels, multiple senders, imperfect channel estimates, energy costs, downstream false-positive costs, and combined folding and compression.
claims.reason: Section VI.C, Limitations and Future Work: The paper explicitly states that future work should study changing contents, measured channels, multiple senders, and combined folding/compression.

claims.text: Channel-aware folding selects the largest qualified view per opportunity without false negatives.
claims.poster_quote: Channel-aware folding selects the largest qualified view per opportunity without false negatives.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity. claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that channel-aware folding selects the largest qualified view per opportunity without false negatives.

claims.text: Channel-aware folding improves efficiency and freshness over complete and compressed baselines under Markov capacity and Rayleigh fading.
claims.poster_quote: Channel-aware folding selects the largest qualified view per opportunity without false negatives. It improves efficiency and freshness over complete and compressed baselines under Markov capacity and Rayleigh fading.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Channel-aware folding improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness relative to complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines when communication opportunities vary substantially. claims.reason: Section I, Abstract: The paper explicitly states that channel-aware folding improves efficiency and freshness over complete and compressed baselines under Markov capacity and Rayleigh fading.

claims.text: Channel-aware folding remains competitive and yields the freshest receiver state under Gilbert-Elliott loss.
claims.poster_quote: Under Gilbert-Elliott loss, it remains competitive and yields the freshest receiver state.

claims.reason: Section V.D, Results Across Datasets and Channel Models: The paper explicitly states that channel-aware folding remains competitive and yields the freshest receiver state under Gilbert-Elliott loss.

claims.text: The sender keeps an unchanged canonical filter and excludes catalog views above the maximum false-positive rate.
claims.poster_quote: The sender keeps an unchanged canonical filter and excludes catalog views above the maximum false-positive rate.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains the canonical filter, constructs a catalog of FPR-qualified folded views, and selects the view with the largest retained length supported at each reporting opportunity. claims.reason: Section I, Introduction: The paper explicitly states that the sender keeps an unchanged canonical filter and excludes catalog views above the maximum false-positive rate.

claims.text: At each opportunity, the sender selects the largest qualified view fitting complete wire capacity.
claims.poster_quote: At each opportunity, it selects the largest qualified view fitting complete wire capacity; under loss, it considers whole-report delivery probability.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: At each reporting opportunity, the sender obtains an estimate of the current communication conditions from the underlying communication system and selects the highest-fidelity FPR-qualified representation supported under those conditions.
claims.reason: Section III.E, Channel-Adaptive Transmission: The paper explicitly states that at each opportunity, the sender selects the largest qualified view fitting complete wire capacity.

claims.text: Under loss, the sender considers whole-report delivery probability.
claims.poster_quote: At each opportunity, it selects the largest qualified view fitting complete wire capacity; under loss, it considers whole-report delivery probability.

claims.reason: Section IV.D, 'Adaptive Transmission Policy' explicitly states that the sender considers the probability of complete-report delivery under the Gilbert–Elliott model.

claims.text: If none can be delivered, the update is deferred.
claims.poster_quote: If none can be delivered, the update is deferred; otherwise, metadata carries retained length and timestamp.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: If no qualified representation can be delivered, the update is deferred.
claims.reason: Section IV.E, 'Channel-Adaptive Transmission' explicitly states that updates are deferred if no qualified representation can be delivered.

claims.text: Metadata carries retained length and timestamp.

claims.text: The receiver installs only complete, newer reports.
